ctx.x: I got very busy in the studios, yeah, because all the arrangers were still in New York: Quincy was still in New York, Billy Byers, Elliot Lawrence, Al Cohn, uhh Manny Albam, Johnny Richards, ah the list is

long, you know, the list is long of the writers, I’m leaving half of them out. But Sauter, Finnegan, um Finkle, uh Billy May, well Billy May was in California, but nevertheless most of the writers were in New York and a lot of the soundtracks were down there. But all of the jingles were done there so I would be working all day, all night and you know I got so busy that Jerome Richardson finally said, “Why don’t you get a flute, man, you know, you don’t have to get very good at it, I mean you already can play the…

items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: There was one record with Bill Evans with two violas, cello, Phil Woods playing clarinet... He used rhythm section.

ctx.x: He also did things for string
quartet and piano bass drums trio. There was one record with Bill Evans with two violas, cello, Phil Woods playing clarinet, Spencer Sinatra playing alto flute and then the rhythm section.
